note: Name + ', my master.' as M2#0 (servant mode); the trailing #152 gives 'Your orders...'.

en: You know what kind of shop this is?
I see hinges and nails for sale.
Figured. No use for a shop like this, eh?
If it's repairs, get your servants to do them.
If you don't need anything, get going.
Either way, you've got nothing to do with me.
You don't need nails or hammers, right? Beat it.
If you don't need anything, get going.
Well, if you want to buy something, I'll sell it.
No, I'm curious about your work.
Hard at it every day. Good work.
You really are a noble or something, huh.
Quit making a fool of me!
You've never had it hard. That's why you can
go "good work" all smug like that!
Still, it'd be fun to make his sort a servant
and work them to the bone. Heh heh heh
Walking all over town is your job, I hear?
You've got your own reasons, I guess.
I've got my reasons for selling hardware, too.
Ask if there's anything you want to know.
If I know the answer, I'll tell you.
If you want hardware, I'll sell it.
Lots of nasty incidents lately, they say.
If you're poking into something, watch yourself.
The shop's not open right now.
Come back later if you want something.
I told you the shop's not open now.
I'm sleepy. And in a foul mood.
I'm sleepy. I'm going to bed.
If you've got time, come on in.
Waking you at all is an act of mercy.

note: Trailing space: a pause splits the sentence mid-phrase (auto_space skips word+word joins).

en: You're the one behind those incidents everyone's talking about
I have come to give you a new life.

en: Wh-what the hell are you saying, bastard?
Don't you go making a fool of me!
I've kept quiet long enough, you—
